prompt_text: What is the best tool for an Airbnb host to set nightly pricing and analyze a market before buying?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- For market research before buying: AirDNA (MarketMinder) is the best single tool for most hosts.
- For ongoing dynamic nightly pricing once you have a listing: PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, or Beyond Pricing — pick one based on how much customization you want (PriceLabs = most customizable; Beyond Pricing = most hands-off; Wheelhouse = strong analytics + A/B testing).
- Use a market tool (AirDNA) + a dynamic-pricing tool (PriceLabs/Wheelhouse/Beyond) together and integrate them with your PMS/channel manager.

Why those choices
- AirDNA (MarketMinder) — industry standard for investment-level short‑term rental data. It gives neighborhood-level ADR, occupancy, seasonality, revenue estimates, historic trends, booking lead times, comparable listings, and portfolio heatmaps so you can model returns and risks before buying.
- PriceLabs — very flexible pricing engine with robust rules, minimum-stay/seasonal controls, and strong demand-based adjustments. Good if you want full control.
- Beyond Pricing — simpler “set-and-forget” dynamic pricing that plugs straight into Airbnb and other channels; less manual rule-building.
- Wheelhouse — a middle ground with advanced analytics, testing features, and good UX for revenue optimization.
- Airbnb Smart Pricing — free but generally less effective and less transparent than the paid tools.

How to choose between PriceLabs / Wheelhouse / Beyond Pricing
- You want fine-grained control of rules, custom minimums, and advanced seasonality: PriceLabs.
- You want to run pricing experiments and see analytics in-app: Wheelhouse.
- You want something automatic and minimal fuss: Beyond Pricing.

Steps I recommend before buying
1. Run AirDNA (MarketMinder) for the exact neighborhood(s) you’re considering. Look at:
   - Historical ADR and occupancy by month (seasonality)
   - Estimated annual revenue for comparable property types
   - Booking lead times and demand curves
   - Listing density and top-performing listings
   - RevPAR and season length
2. Cross-check with at least one other data source (AllTheRooms, Transparent, InsideAirbnb for supply-side snapshots).
3. Model cash flow: include mortgage, taxes, insurance, utilities, cleaning, management fees, furnishing, vacancy buffer, and capex.
4. Check local regulations, HOA rules and short-term rental licensing.
5. If the numbers look good, set up a trial with a pricing tool (PriceLabs/Wheelhouse/Beyond) and integrate with your channel manager or Airbnb to simulate or run pricing for a few listings to see uplift.

Other things to consider
- Integration with your PMS/channel manager (Hostaway, Guesty, Lodgify, etc.) — makes automation smoother.
- Fee model: some pricing tools charge a subscription per listing, others a percent of revenue; try free trials before committing.
- Data limitations: no tool is perfect; use multiple inputs and conservative assumptions.

If you want, tell me the city/neighborhood you’re looking at and your property type (studio/1BR/2BR), and I can suggest specific metrics to check and a quick shortlist of comparable listings to evaluate.
